subject: How to plot only subjects with multiple observations?

messages.author: 473c4ce8ca8f75f2
messages.subject: How to plot only subjects with multiple observations?
parts:
Hello

I have a data frame that has data on about 25 people on about 20 variables of interest.
Each person is measured up to 10 times, but some people are measured only once or twice,
and, even for the people who are measured more times, some variables are missing for nearly
all cases.

I am exploring the data using qplot:

qplot(days, C3a, facets = ~Patient_Name, data = multvisit, geom = c("point", "smooth"),
main = 'C3a over time in people with more than 2 visits',
xlab = 'Days since 9/25/06')

but this produces plots for all people. How can I produce plots just for people with 3 or
more non-missing observations?


thanks

Peter

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: How to plot only subjects with multiple observations?
parts:
Hi Peter,

You could use plyr to add a column that counts the number of
observations and then subset on that:

multvisit <- ddply(multvisit, "Patient_Name", transform, n = sum(is.na(C3a))
subset(multvisit, n > 3)

If you have many columns like this, it might be easier to melt the
data first, then compute the counts

multm <- melt(multvisit, id = c("Patient_Name", "days"), na.rm = T)
multm <- ddply(mult, c("Patient_Name", "days"), transform, n = seq_along(days))

qplot(days, value, data = subset(multm, n > 3 && variable == "C3a"))

Hadley
